key_insight: This paper shows that full-duplex speech agents need more than a binary choice of “keep talking” or “stop.” It introduces a third, human-like behavior: continuing to speak while adapting in real time to what the listener just said.
problem_solved: Existing full-duplex evaluations miss in-turn adaptation, where a speaker incorporates a listener’s cue such as a missing word, correction, or clarification without yielding the floor. The paper addresses how to evaluate and distinguish these nuanced responses in overlapping speech.
method: Introduces Duplex Cue, an evaluation framework for in-turn adaptation in full-duplex voice agents.
Separates listener intent into categories such as backchannel, collaboration, and interruption.
Assesses whether the speaker should continue, adapt, or yield when overlap occurs.
impact: This matters because real conversational AI must handle interruptions and corrections naturally, not just avoid talking over users. For practitioners, Duplex Cue provides a more realistic benchmark for building voice agents that sound responsive, collaborative, and human-like.
visual_elements: Three-way decision flow: continue vs adapt vs yield
Overlapping speech timeline showing speaker and listener cues
Comparison chart contrasting binary evaluation vs Duplex Cue
paper_title: Continue, Adapt, or Yield: In-Turn Adaptation to Overlapping Speech in Full-Duplex Agents
paper_authors: Yunqi Lu, Tyler Baumgartner, Nikhil Johri, Brandon Tai, Candice Fan
